'''Eduard L. Stiefel''' (21 April 1909 – 25 November 1978) was a [[Switzerland|Swiss]] [[mathematician]]. Together with [[Cornelius Lanczos]] and [[Magnus Hestenes]], he invented the [[conjugate gradient method]], and gave what is now understood to be a partial construction of the [[Stiefel–Whitney class]]es of a [[real vector bundle]], thus co-founding the study of [[characteristic classes]].

==Early life and education==
Eduard Stiefel was born on 21 April 1909 in [[Zürich]]. His father was the painter and graphic artist [[Eduard Stiefel (painter)|Eduard Stiefel]], after whom he was named.

Stiefel attended schools in his hometown and from 1927 to 1931 studied mathematics and physics at the [[ETH Zurich|Swiss Federal Institute of Technology (ETH Zurich)]]. He graduated with distinction in 1931 and continued his studies in [[Hamburg]] and [[Göttingen]]. In 1935 he received his doctorate from ETH under [[Heinz Hopf]], with a dissertation entitled ''Richtungsfelder und Fernparallelismus in n-dimensionalen Mannigfaltigkeiten'' (Direction fields and distant parallelism in n-dimensional manifolds). After a period as a research assistant, Stiefel completed his [[habilitation]], becoming a [[Privatdozent]] in 1942 and a full professor at [[ETH Zurich]] in 1943.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eduard Stiefel 1909–1978 |url=http://www.library.ethz.ch/Ressourcen/Digitale-Kollektionen/Kurzportraets/Eduard-Stiefel-1909-bis-1978 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131203054309/http://www.library.ethz.ch/Ressourcen/Digitale-Kollektionen/Kurzportraets/Eduard-Stiefel-1909-bis-1978 |archive-date=3 December 2013 |website=ETH Zurich Library}}</ref>

== Career ==
Stiefel's early research was in [[topology]], including work on the topology of [[Lie group|Lie groups]] and [[Fiber bundle|fibre bundles]].<ref>{{cite book |last1=Milnor |first1=John |title=[[Characteristic Classes]] |last2=Stasheff |first2=James |publisher=Princeton University Press |year=1974 |isbn=978-0-691-08122-9 |series=Annals of Mathematics Studies |volume=76|mr=0440554}}</ref> A class of [[Characteristic class|characteristic classes]], the [[Stiefel–Whitney class]], bears his name.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Fu |first1=Joseph H. G. |last2=McCrory |first2=Clint |year=1997 |title=Stiefel–Whitney classes and the conormal cycle of a singular variety |journal=Transactions of the American Mathematical Society |volume=349 |issue=2 |pages=809–835 |doi=10.1090/S0002-9947-97-01815-1 |arxiv=dg-ga/9508010}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal |last=McTague |first=Carl |year=2011 |title=Stiefel–Whitney numbers for singular varieties |journal=Mathematical Proceedings of the Cambridge Philosophical Society |volume=150 |issue=2 |pages=273–289 |doi=10.1017/S0305004110000630 |arxiv=1004.4348 |bibcode=2011MPCPS.150..273M }}</ref> His classification of fibre bundles over [[N-sphere|spheres]] also found application in the classification of algebras, as discussed by [[Friedrich Hirzebruch]] in [[Heinz-Dieter Ebbinghaus]] et al., ''Zahlen'' (Springer, 1992).<ref>{{cite book |last1=Ebbinghaus |first1=Heinz-Dieter |title=Numbers |last2=Hirzebruch |first2=Friedrich |publisher=Springer |year=1991 |isbn=978-0-387-97497-2 |series=Graduate Texts in Mathematics |volume=123 |location=New York |chapter=Division Algebras and Topology |display-authors=et al.}}</ref>

Besides his academic pursuits, Stiefel was also active as a military officer, rising to the rank of colonel in the Swiss army during [[World War II]].

He later turned entirely to [[numerical mathematics]]. After achieving his full professorship at [[ETH Zurich]] in 1943, Stiefel founded the [[Seminar for Applied Mathematics|Institute for Applied Mathematics]] in 1948, which he also directed. The objective of the new institute was to design and construct an electronic computer (the ''Elektronische Rechenmaschine der ETH'', or [[ERMETH]]). For this, Stiefel located a [[Zuse Z4|Z4]] computer by [[Konrad Zuse]] in Bavaria in 1949; the machine was leased from Zuse and restored to working order for ETH. This made ETH Zurich the first university on the European continent to operate a programmable computing machine, which was used, among other tasks, to calculate the [[Gravity dam|gravity wall]] of a dam. Stiefel later sent his assistants [[Heinz Rutishauser]] and [[Ambros Speiser]] to the United States to study computing machines, which led to the development of ETH's own computer, [[ERMETH]], in operation from 1955 to 1963.

He also spent a year in the [[United States]] commencing in August, 1951. During this time, he met [[Magnus Hestenes]] and other scientists at the [[National Bureau of Standards]] and these professional associations served him during the remainder of his career at [[Zurich]].

Stiefel also worked on [[celestial mechanics]],<ref>{{Cite book |last1=Stiefel |first1=Eduard |title=Linear and regular celestial mechanics: perturbed two-body motion, numerical methods, canonical theory |last2=Stiefel |first2=Eduard |last3=Scheifele |first3=Gerhard |date=1971 |publisher=Springer |isbn=978-0-387-05119-2 |series=Die Grundlehren der mathematischen Wissenschaften in Einzeldarstellungen |location=Berlin}}</ref> in particular the calculation of satellite orbits, and more broadly on [[perturbation theory]].<ref>{{Citation |title=New Methods of Celestial Mechanics |date=2012-03-20 |pages=i–ii |editor-last=Vrbik |editor-first=Jan |url=http://www.eurekaselect.com/node/51960 |access-date=2026-06-07 |publisher=BENTHAM SCIENCE PUBLISHERS |doi=10.2174/97816080518781100101000i |isbn=9781608051878|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=New Methods of Celestial Mechanics |url=https://benthambooks.com/book/9781608051878/foreword/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=benthambooks.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Roa |first1=Javier |last2=Urrutxua |first2=Hodei |last3=Peláez |first3=Jesús |date=2016-07-01 |title=Stability and chaos in Kustaanheimo–Stiefel space induced by the Hopf fibration |journal=Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society |language=en |volume=459 |issue=3 |pages=2444–2454 |doi=10.1093/mnras/stw780 |doi-access=free |issn=0035-8711|arxiv=1604.06673 }}</ref> A regularisation method developed by him and Paul Kustaanheimo, applying [[Spinor|spinors]] and a transformation in four-dimensional space, bears his name – The [[Kustaanheimo–Stiefel regularization]]. Stiefel received research contracts from [[European Space Agency|ESA]] (and its predecessor [[ESRO]]) and from [[NASA]]. From 1966 to 1970 he served as president of the Swiss Committee for Space Research.

Stiefel, who edited [[Issai Schur]]'s lectures on representation theory at ETH Zurich in 1936,<ref>{{Citation |last1=Puntanen |first1=Simo |title=Historical Introduction: Issai Schur and the Early Development of the Schur Complement |date=2005 |volume=4 |pages=1–16 |editor-last=Zhang |editor-first=Fuzhen |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/0-387-24273-2_1 |access-date=2026-06-07 |chapter=The Schur Complement and Its Applications |place=New York |publisher=Springer-Verlag |language=en |doi=10.1007/0-387-24273-2_1 |isbn=978-0-387-24271-2 |last2=Styan |first2=George P. H.|url-access=subscription }}</ref> also authored a book on [[group theory]] and one on [[descriptive geometry]].<ref>{{cite book |last=Schur |first=Issai |title=Die algebraischen Grundlagen der Darstellungstheorie der Gruppen |year=1936 |editor-last=Stiefel |editor-first=Eduard}}</ref>

In 1952 he developed the [[conjugate gradient method]] in [[numerical linear algebra]] together with Magnus Hestenes.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Hestenes |first1=M.R. |last2=Stiefel |first2=E. |date=1952-12-01 |title=Methods of conjugate gradients for solving linear systems |url=https://nvlpubs.nist.gov/nistpubs/jres/049/jresv49n6p409_A1b.pdf |journal=Journal of Research of the National Bureau of Standards |language=en |volume=49 |issue=6 |pages=409 |doi=10.6028/jres.049.044 |issn=0091-0635}}</ref>

In 1956 he served as president of the [[Swiss Mathematical Society]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Organisation » Past Presidents {{!}} The Swiss Mathematical Society |url=https://math.ch/organisation/past-presidents/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=math.ch}}</ref><ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Eduard Stiefel - Biography |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Stiefel/ |access-date=2026-06-07 |website=Maths History |language=en}}</ref> From 1970 to 1974 he was president of the [[Gesellschaft für Angewandte Mathematik und Mechanik|Society for Applied Mathematics and Mechanics]] (GAMM).<ref name=":0" />

Stiefel was a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] and the [[German National Academy of Sciences Leopoldina|Leopoldina]], and received honorary doctorates from [[KU Leuven]] (1971), the [[University of Würzburg]] (1974), and the [[Technische Universität Braunschweig|University of Braunschweig]] (1975).<ref name=":1">{{cite web |title=Eduard Stiefel (1909–1978) |url=https://mathshistory.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Stiefel/ |website=MacTutor History of Mathematics |publisher=University of St Andrews}}</ref> In 1968 he held a visiting professorship at the [[Université libre de Bruxelles]].<ref name=":1" /> Stiefel also served as a colonel of artillery in the [[Swiss Army]] and was a member of the Zürich city council from 1958 to 1966, representing the [[Ring of Independents|Landesring der Unabhängigen]].<ref name=":1" />

In 1954 he delivered a plenary lecture at the [[International Congress of Mathematicians]] in [[Amsterdam]], entitled "Recent developments in relaxation techniques".<ref>{{cite book |last=Stiefel |first=Eduard |title=Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Amsterdam, 1954 |publisher=North-Holland |year=1957 |location=Amsterdam |chapter=Recent developments in relaxation techniques}}</ref>
[[File:Eduard Stiefel Grabstein Friedhof Witikon Zürich.jpg|thumb|Stiefel's grave at Witikon Cemetery, [[Zurich]]]]
Among Stiefel's doctoral students were [[Ambros Speiser]], [[Peter Henrici (mathematician)|Peter Henrici]], {{ill|Urs Kirchgraber|de}}, {{ill|Fritz-Rudolf Güntsch|de}}, [[Max Rössler]], and Jörg Waldvogel.<ref>{{cite web |title=Eduard L. Stiefel |url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=19976 |website=Mathematics Genealogy Project |publisher=North Dakota State University}}</ref>
